questions.stem: A Spark join between a 2-billion-row fact table and a 500-row lookup table is slow because both sides are shuffled. What helps?

options.text: Collect the large table to the driver
Broadcast the small table so each executor has a copy and the large table isn't shuffled
Repartition the small table into 2,000 partitions

questions.explanation: A broadcast join sends the small table to every executor, avoiding a shuffle of the large one.

questions.stem: Which Fabric feature can speed up Spark queries by running them on a native vectorized engine, without code changes?
questions.explanation: The native execution engine runs supported Spark operations natively on a vectorized engine.

questions.stem: Queries on a large table always filter on EventDate. How can the table's layout reduce the data read?

options.text: Store it as one huge file
Z-order the table on EventDate with OPTIMIZE ZORDER BY, so filters skip files

questions.explanation: Z-ordering colocates rows with similar EventDate values, which tightens each file's min/max statistics so Spark skips files outside the filter.

questions.stem: A notebook reads the same expensive DataFrame in several later steps. What can avoid recomputing it each time?

options.text: Cache or persist the DataFrame after it's built

questions.explanation: Caching keeps the computed DataFrame in memory or on disk, so later actions reuse it.

questions.stem: The Native Execution Engine is enabled, but a notebook step that applies a Python user-defined function doesn't get faster. Why?

options.text: The engine only accelerates writes, not reads
The engine doesn't support UDFs, so those operations fall back to the JVM engine
The engine needs V-Order on the source table
The engine only works with Fabric runtime 1.2

questions.explanation: The Native Execution Engine doesn't support UDFs, array_contains or structured streaming, and those operations fall back to the JVM engine automatically. It isn't available on Runtime 1.2.

questions.stem: A new workspace runs mostly read-heavy Spark queries. New workspaces default to the writeHeavy profile. Which code switches the session to a read-optimized Spark profile?
questions.explanation: Resource profiles are set with spark.fabric.resourceProfile; readHeavyForSpark targets read-heavy Spark workloads. writeHeavy is the default that disables V-Order.

questions.stem: A Spark job's shuffle stages create far more tiny tasks than the data needs. Which setting, with a default of 200, should you tune based on data volume?
questions.explanation: spark.sql.shuffle.partitions defaults to 200 and should be tuned to the data volume. maxPartitionBytes tunes reads, not shuffles.

questions.stem: Several notebooks run one after another with the same lakehouse, environment and Spark settings, and each one waits for a new session to start. What reduces this startup time?

options.text: Turn on V-Order for each table
Increase the default session timeout to 24 hours
Enable high concurrency mode so that the notebooks share one session

questions.explanation: High concurrency mode lets notebooks with the same lakehouse, environment and configs share a session and removes startup overhead. Active sessions use CU, so stop them when idle.

questions.stem: You want Spark to estimate the ideal target file size for Delta tables from table heuristics and re-evaluate it at each OPTIMIZE. Which setting do you turn on?
questions.explanation: Adaptive target file size uses Delta table heuristics to estimate the ideal file size and re-evaluates it at each OPTIMIZE; it's recommended but not on by default.

questions.stem: Which two things does Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) do at run time? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: Install missing Python libraries in the session
Remove unreferenced files older than seven days
Apply V-Order to files written by the query

questions.explanation: AQE uses runtime statistics to coalesce post-shuffle partitions, convert sort-merge joins to broadcast joins and apply skew-join optimization. V-Order, VACUUM and library installation are unrelated.
